turns.t: Hi. My mum said I had to come. I don't want to be here. ~
Thanks for coming anyway, that took some guts. What did she say was going on? ~
That I won't go to school. But it's not that I won't, I can't.
Tell me what happens when you try.
My heart goes crazy, my stomach drops, and I feel sick. Sometimes I can't breathe properly, and I sit on the stairs and cry.
Which part of school is hardest? ~
The classroom, being looked at. Presentations. And lunch, where there's nobody I know. ~
How long has this been going on?
Since September. I've missed about six weeks.
Are you sleeping all right? ~
Not great. My mind goes round at night. ~
Do you ever have thoughts of harming yourself, or not wanting to be here?
No. No, nothing like that. I'm just scared.
Thank you for telling me. Do you take any medicines at the moment?
Propranolol, 10 mg, when I'm really bad. My doctor in Delhi gave me them, and I only take them when I need to.
Any allergies to medicines, to anything?
No, nothing.
Is there anyone in the family who has anxiety?
My mum does. She has panic attacks. She says it runs in the family.
Who do you live with, and what year are you in?
Mum, dad and my little sister. I'm in Year 10.
And what do you do in your free time?
Games, mostly. Four, five hours a day. I don't go out much.
Okay. Did you fill in the questionnaire the receptionist gave you, about how you've been feeling?
Yeah, I already did it in the waiting room.
I've read it. Your score shows a moderate level of anxiety, which fits what you've told me. ~
I knew it. ~
This is very common in teenagers and it's treatable. Avoiding school makes it worse in the long run, so we want to get you back gradually. ~
I can't. ~
Not all at once. We'd start small, with an agreed plan with your school, one lesson, a quiet room, a person you can go to.
Maybe. ~
I'd also like to arrange a blood test, to rule out any physical cause for the racing heart, like your thyroid.
Fine. I don't like needles. ~
I know. We can use numbing cream. ~
Okay. ~
And I'd like to refer you to the young people's mental health service for talking therapy, which works really well for this.
Do I have to talk to a stranger? ~
Yes, but they're kind, and they've seen hundreds of people like you. ~
Okay. ~
I'd like to see you again in two weeks, to see how you're getting on, and you can bring your mum if you want to.
Alright. ~
